info.name: Flight Operations - distributed tests (SIDIS PL3)
info.description:
Tests from the Week 3 practical session (PL3 p.15-17): local data access, forwarding, resilience, load distribution, edge cases.

**Before running**: start two instances in stub mode (built-in aircraft/route data, so flights can be created without the other two services):

    ./scripts/run-local.sh --stub

Select the environment "Flight Ops - local (2 instances)" and run the whole collection. Folder 03 (resilience) runs last: it stops instance 2 by itself, checks the failure behaviour, and waits for run-local.sh to restart instance 2 (the whole run takes about a minute).

Postman on the web (browser) reaches localhost only through the Postman Desktop Agent.

item.name: 09 Sharding by aircraft
item.description: P1 p.15 data-based sharding: every aircraft has an owner instance (rendezvous hashing over the instance names) that stores all of its flights. A booking sent to another instance is forwarded to the owner (X-Stored-On), and the owner's per-aircraft lock prevents double-booking even when the requests arrive at different instances.

item.name: 03 Resilience - instance 2 is stopped and restarted
item.description:
PL3 p.16 test 03 and PL3 p.14 (automatic recovery). Runs last. Needs the instances started with scripts/run-local.sh --stub (stub = test mode, where an ADMIN may shut an instance down over HTTP; the script restarts a stopped instance after 10 s).

1. Stops instance 2 (POST /actuator/shutdown) and waits until it is gone.
2. Instance 1 still serves its own data; data stored only on instance 2 gives 404 (PL3 p.11) with "could not be reached"; the circuit breaker reports instance 2 as down.
3. Waits for instance 2 to come back (up to 90 s) and checks that instance 1 trusts it again and forwards to it again. The flight stored on instance 2 is still there: its data survived the restart (PostgreSQL).

If instance 2 cannot be stopped (not in stub mode) the tests of step 2 are skipped; stop it by hand and run this folder again.

exec: // wait (max 20 s) until instance 2 really stops answering
pm.test('instance 2 is down', () => pm.expect.fail('instance 2 still answers after 20 s'));
pm.test.skip("SKIPPED: instance 2 is still running (could not be stopped) - stop it by hand, then run folder 03 again", () => {});
pm.test.skip("SKIPPED: instance 2 is still running (could not be stopped) - stop it by hand, then run folder 03 again", () => {});
